questions.questionText: What does dropout actually do during training?
options: It permanently removes weak neurons from the network
It randomly zeroes out a fraction of neurons on each training step, preventing neurons from co-adapting to very specific combinations
It increases the learning rate over time
It only affects the output layer
questions.correctAnswer: It randomly zeroes out a fraction of neurons on each training step, preventing neurons from co-adapting to very specific combinations
questions.explanation: By randomly disabling different neurons each step, dropout forces the network to learn features that are useful without relying on very specific neuron combinations, reducing overfitting.

questions.questionText: What problem does batch normalization primarily address?
options: It removes the need for an activation function
The shifting distribution of layer inputs during training (internal covariate shift), which makes deep networks slower and more sensitive to train
It replaces the need for a loss function
It only matters for convolutional layers, never fully-connected ones
questions.correctAnswer: The shifting distribution of layer inputs during training (internal covariate shift), which makes deep networks slower and more sensitive to train
questions.explanation: By re-centering and re-scaling each layer's inputs using current batch statistics, batch norm keeps input distributions stable, enabling higher learning rates and more robust training.

questions.questionText: In early stopping, what signal tells you it's time to stop training?
options: Validation loss starting to increase even while training loss keeps decreasing
A fixed number of epochs, regardless of performance
questions.correctAnswer: Validation loss starting to increase even while training loss keeps decreasing
questions.explanation: That divergence between improving training loss and worsening validation loss is the signature of the model starting to memorize training data instead of generalizing — the same overfitting signal from the Classical ML course's bias-variance lesson.
